root_cause.text: The virtio vsock receive credit check in virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() accounted only packet payload length in vvs->buf_used/rx_bytes and ignored per-skb queue overhead, so zero-length VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM packets that bypass coalescing could be enqueued without consuming the buf_alloc limit.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that "virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() checks vvs->rx_bytes + len > vvs->buf_alloc" and that for "len == 0 and VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM, a very large number of packets can be queued because vvs->rx_bytes stays at 0"; the patch fixes this by adding `u64 skb_overhead = (skb_queue_len(&vvs->rx_queue) + 1) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0);` and checking `skb_overhead + vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Account for skb queue overhead in virtio vsock receive buffer limit checks to prevent underestimating buffer usage.
intent_record.what: The function virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() was modified to introduce a new local variable, `u64 skb_overhead`, computed as `(skb_queue_len(&vvs->rx_queue) + 1) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0)`, and the existing capacity check was changed from `vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc` to `skb_overhead + vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, receive-buffer admission now accounts not only for payload bytes already used plus the incoming packet length, but also for per-skb memory overhead based on the queued packet count. This prevents accepting packets when skb metadata overhead would cause actual memory usage to exceed the allocated buffer budget.

grouping_result.intent: Account for skb queue overhead in virtio vsock receive buffer limit checks to prevent underestimating buffer usage.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes virtio vsock receive credit/buffer accounting by including skb queue overhead in buffer limit checks, preventing zero-length packets from bypassing buf_alloc usage accounting.

candidates.rationale: This receive credit check enforces the buffer limit using only the packet payload length. It omits per-skb queue overhead, allowing zero-length packets to pass the limit check without consuming buf_alloc.
This accounting updates received-buffer usage based only on payload length, ignoring skb overhead. As a result, queued zero-length packets are not charged against the receive buffer budget.

vuln_statements.explanation: This receive credit check compares the buffer budget against only the incoming payload length. Because it ignores per-skb queue overhead, zero-length packets can be accepted without consuming the buf_alloc limit, enabling unbounded enqueueing.

This accounting statement increments tracked receive usage using only payload length. It fails to charge skb overhead, so zero-length packets do not increase the tracked buffer usage and can accumulate despite the intended receive buffer limit.

In this commit, `virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt()` was changed to take only a payload length: `static bool virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt(struct virtio_vsock_sock *vvs, u32 len)` and it checks `if (vvs->rx_bytes + len > vvs->buf_alloc) return false;` then `vvs->rx_bytes += len;`. The enqueue path confirms this behavior: `can_enqueue = virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt(vvs, len);`. Therefore, a zero-length packet (`len == 0`), including zero-length `VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM` packets, would not consume any of `rx_bytes` and could be queued despite still allocating an skb. That matches the stated root cause. The fix is not present here because there is no accounting for skb/truesize/overhead or any special handling for zero-length packets that bypass coalescing; the code explicitly tracks only payload length.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant receive-credit accounting logic is fully shown. In `virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt()`, the code checks only payload length: `if (vvs->rx_bytes + skb->len > vvs->buf_alloc) return false;` and then `vvs->rx_bytes += skb->len;`. This means queued memory overhead from each skb is not charged against `buf_alloc`. That matches the root cause: accounting only packet payload length in `rx_bytes`/buffer usage. The enqueue path in `virtio_transport_recv_enqueue()` can still queue packets even when `len` is zero, because it calls `virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt(vvs, skb)` before deciding whether to coalesce, and `len` comes from `hdr->len` while `skb->len` may be zero for a zero-length packet. The code also increments `msg_count` on `VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM` packets (`if (le32_to_cpu(hdr->flags) & VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM) vvs->msg_count++;`), so zero-length SEQ_EOM packets are meaningful and may be queued. Coalescing is bypassed when the last queued packet is already EOM due to `!(le32_to_cpu(last_hdr->flags) & VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM)`, so such zero-length packets can accumulate as separate skbs without consuming `buf_alloc` under this accounting. There is no fix here that charges skb overhead on enqueue; instead, the dequeue-side `virtio_transport_dec_rx_pkt()` uses `len = skb_headroom(skb) - sizeof(struct virtio_vsock_hdr) - skb->len; vvs->rx_bytes -= len; vvs->fwd_cnt += len;`, which is not matching the enqueue accounting and does not represent a proper enqueue-side fix for skb overhead. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not.
